why: RFC-0010's zero-copy path. rcl/rclcpp borrow a TYPED message the middleware owns (`LoanedMessage<T>`, `borrow_loaned_message`, `publish_loaned_message`, `return_loaned_message_from_publisher`); ours is a TOKEN over a byte range (`loan`/`commit`/`discard` on the publisher, `borrow`/`release` on the subscription) because C has no templates and the wrapper would need an allocator to own. NOTE the verbs differ as well as the shape, and only the shape has a reason -- W5 should decide whether `loan`/`commit`/`discard` should read `borrow_loaned_message`/`publish_loaned_message`/`return_loaned_message`.
